message: remind me in 20 minutes to stretch
comment: MIRRORS the SHAPE of S9's first definition-of-done line (docs/plans/rebuild/slice-09-scheduling.md, 'remind me in two minutes to stretch'): a relative reminder must become a timer ROW through create_timer — never a promise ('I'll remind you in two minutes' with no call, the deferral/bare-intent shape), never a false denial ('I can't set reminders', which guards.capability_claim_check now contradicts because create_timer is registered), and never an offer handed back ('Want me to set a reminder?', the _SET_REMINDER offer class). The message is RELATIVE on purpose: a relative reminder needs no household timezone, so this case is gradeable on a fresh instance whose nova.timezone was never set (an absolute time would be refused there with the stated no-timezone sentence, and the case would measure the install, not the model). The delay is TWENTY minutes, not the DoD's two: evals run in-process beside the real scheduler loop and the scratch person is deleted only after the case ends, so a case that outlives the delay (a slow local model, tool rounds, scoring) would let the timer actually fire — a 'Reminder: stretch' turn into the scratch conversation and a device_notify to every connected paired device, an eval showing up on the owner's desktop (memory: journal-probe-noise). Twenty minutes is far past any case's runtime; the contract (a create_timer span succeeded) is identical. tool_succeeded('create_timer') is the direct trace fact that a row exists — the executor validates through schedule.validate and persists through timers.create, so a succeeded span IS a persisted timer. The scratch person's timer cascades away with the person (timers.person_id ON DELETE CASCADE) at cleanup, so an eval never leaves a reminder that would later fire into nobody's chat. MECHANICAL, not a proxy. Added 2026-09-07 with the S9 corpus bump (6 -> 7). suite_version moved 7 -> 8 because four S12 agent cases joined the suite (delegates-the-write-to-an-agent, no-fabricated-agent-work, no-disowned-delegation-tool, scope-limit-is-not-a-disowned-capability; 2026-09-09).
